note: PR #308 CI repair. This registry REPLACES a blanket 'no model asset may exist anywhere' rule (__tests__/mirrorExtractionContainment.test.js) that predated Live VTO. That rule was written for the Mirror Selfie containment contract, where the only correct answer is an OS-resident runtime (ML Kit's bundled pose detector on Android, Apple Vision on iOS) and a checked-in model would mean somebody vendored one by hand. Live VTO N1-E then introduced a REQUIRED bundled on-device model: the approved architecture is offline inference with no runtime download and no cloud inference, which is impossible to satisfy without shipping the weights. A blanket prohibition and a mandatory bundled model cannot both be right, so the prohibition becomes an explicit, byte-bound, fail-closed allowlist. Nothing is broadened: an unlisted model asset still fails, a listed model whose bytes changed fails, and `modelFreeModules` below makes the Mirror module's original prohibition CATEGORICAL rather than incidental.

policy.denyReason: Any tracked file matching modelAssetExtensions is a violation unless an approvedModels record names its exact path AND its sha256 matches the committed bytes.
policy.extensionListProvenance: Copied verbatim from the regex the superseded blanket test used (/\.(tflite|mlmodel|mlmodelc|onnx|pb|pt|task)$/) so this repair cannot silently narrow what counts as a model asset. Adding a format here widens detection; removing one is a weakening and must be justified in its own change.
policy.wildcardRationale: Approval is per-artifact and byte-bound. A glob such as '**/*.task' or a directory-level approval would let any future model land unreviewed, which is exactly the failure mode the superseded blanket rule existed to prevent.
policy.modelFreeModulesRationale: STRENGTHENING, not a carve-out. The Mirror Selfie / Closet PII module must use OS-resident runtimes only -- see __tests__/mirrorIosVisionParity.test.js and __tests__/closetMediaPrivacyAutolinking.test.js, which already forbid a vendored model inside this module. Listing it here means a model asset under this prefix fails EVEN IF someone adds an approvedModels record for it: the registry cannot be used to authorize one. Under the superseded blanket rule this protection was only incidental (everything was banned); here it is stated and separately enforced.

approvedModels.purposeDetail: N1-E on-device pose estimation. Produces BodyFrame landmarks that drive the native garment deformation/renderer entirely on device.
approvedModels.licenseEvidenceNote: Framework license read from the published tasks-vision-1.0.0.pom <licenses> block; model/weights license from the MediaPipe project's own NOTICE bundled in tasks-core-1.0.0.aar. Verified as SEPARATE items at N1-E integration time and recorded there with the method used. This registry deliberately does NOT re-verify licences at CI time: a guard that reaches the network to check a licence would be an internet-dependent test and would fail closed for the wrong reason on an offline runner.
approvedModels.approvedBy: N1-E mission (real local perception), owner-directed; CI governance added by the PR #308 CI-green repair

approvedModels.purposeDetail: iOS native-runtime catch-up: on-device pose estimation, same purpose as the Android record above. Produces BodyFrame landmarks that drive the native garment deformation/renderer entirely on device.
approvedModels.licenseEvidenceNote: Same governed model file as live-vto-pose-landmarker-lite (Android) -- byte-identical, sha256 verified equal at copy time (see docs/vto-live-bridge-contract.md). License terms already verified there; not re-verified independently for this record since it is the same artifact.
